observation.visible_scene: A calm, slow-moving forest river or pond framed by dense green deciduous trees on both banks. The water surface is glassy and acts as a mirror, reflecting the tree canopies and a pale, bright gap of sky visible at the top center. A single grey rock protrudes from the water just left of the center line, with a smaller rock near the middle. A fallen log lies along the right bank, and a few leafy branches intrude into the right foreground. Lighting is soft and even, suggesting an overcast or shaded midday.
visible_changes: The overall composition, framing, and the position of the rock, trees, and sky gap remain fixed from frame 1 to frame 41, indicating no camera pan, tilt, or zoom.

The water's reflection and surface texture show only very slight, low-amplitude shimmering/ripple variation between frames, consistent with a near-still surface rather than any flowing or disturbed motion.
Foreground leaves on the right and tree foliage appear essentially unchanged; no clear, sustained sway or object movement is discernible across the sampled frames.
No person, animal, or moving object enters or exits the scene during the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether any wind or current exists is not determinable from these frames; the clip neither shows an onset nor a cessation of motion.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.67s (e.g., weather change, a disturbance to the water) are outside the excerpt and remain unknown.
uncertain_details: The faint differences in reflection detail between frames could be real micro-ripples or simply video-compression noise; the magnitude is too small to confirm actual water motion.
Any leaf movement is at the threshold of detectability and cannot be confidently separated from static rendering.
